questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As a psychology student, a crucial consideration in selecting my study destination was the availability of English-taught programs. Canada had always been at the of my list of preferred study destinations, so it made sense for me to pursue my studies there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. Prior to my arrival, the university communicated via multiple emails, providing detailed guidance on where to seek information or assistance if required any. They also had an international office where they offered support and guidance.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had some trouble with the courses that required approval by KU, so I received assistance from their international office to navigate through the process. The university also organised an international orientation week tailored for international and exchange students, featuring various gathering and networking opportunities to connect with fellow international peers.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was actually quite hard, especially for a short amount of time (1 semester). Most rental properties are typically looking for a commitment to a one-year lease term. And the list provided by the host university had the same issue. Also, I didn't really know where else to look - so it was definitely a process. There's also a lot of scammers - so beware!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Again, there can be many scammers so be careful! But personally, I found it kinda nice to live off-campus. That being said, roommates can sometimes be tricky, so make sure you know who you'll be sharing living space with.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Before my arrival, I received an email from the International office as Western containing a link to the courses offered for that term. I then had to inform them of the courses I wished to take, and the international office handled registration process on my behalf. As an exchange student, I wasn't able to register the courses independently - but it worked out fine.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The International office was available to help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Navigating the course requirements was a bit challenging since Western really put focus on prerequisites and antirequisites, and KU has specific course requirements too. Nevertheless, it worked out in the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure registrations and approvals are completed before your arrival. While it's technically possible to register after you arrive, it's honestly best to avoid that because the approval process at KU can take some time. Additionally, it's important to note that desirable courses at the host university can fill up quickly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was fine - I didn't find it overly challenging, and they offered very interesting and engaging courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The course structure leans more towards lectures, with relatively less emphasis on group work or discussions, which suited my preferences. The final grade is typically a combination of assignments, participation in discussion forums (in some courses), midterms (multiple-choice), final exams (multiple-choice), and semester projects (some courses). Personally, I find this grading style preferable as it encourages and motivates continuous study and engagement throughout the semester. Additionally, they schedule lectures and classes at significantly different times compared to KU. For instance, in some courses, I had lectures scheduled from 7 pm to 10 pm - I personally didn't mind.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Clinical psychology, Maladjusted mind, Forensic psychology, and Research methods

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Forensic psychology was honestly so interesting. We worked with real-world police cases and investigations, delved into criminology, and explored the complexities of psychopaths and the criminal mind. Personally, I found it incredibly fascinating.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Phone bill was a little higher than in Denmark, but it was fine. And grocery shopping is a bit more expensive than in Denmark - but you get used to it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were so many different activities you can participate in, ranging from different music genres, dance styles, and sports to ethnic and religious clubs. During the first few weeks of the semester, they host a clubs week where you can learn about all the clubs available!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Honestly, there's something for everyone based on their interests. For instance, I'm a fan of K-pop, so I joined the K-pop club. I really felt like there was a club for every interest. But you're not limited to just one club - I was a part of multiple clubs simultaneously.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you have the opportunity, I highly recommend exploring other parts of Canada. If not, at least consider visiting Toronto and Niagara Falls; but if you're there during the fall semester, I'd suggest visiting Niagara Falls in the fall rather than winter - it can be a bit grey in the winter. London is a great town, but it is mainly a university town, so a lot is revolved around the university - which is great, but if you wish to see more of Canada then definitely go to other regions. You can easily travel to Toronto with the Flixbus for only 20 CAD! Also, I would definitely recommend to go skiing at Boler Mountain in the winter. Above all, just enjoy your time and try to step out of your comfort zone - you'll find that there are a lot of great people out there.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was actually not as difficult as I expected. As I mentioned earlier, London is a university town so you'll be spending a lot of time on campus. However, Western University really prioritizes diversity, which made it easier for me to feel like I belonged.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Again, there are plenty of clubs you can join to meet people - so I would definitely recommend giving those a try. But most importantly, just have fun and don't be afraid to step out of your comfort zone.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I can't think of anything particularly challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I was pleasantly surprised by how open and friendly everyone was. In Denmark, people can sometimes be a bit reserved, but I didn't encounter that in London at all.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Step out of your comfort zone! Western University offers a diverse community, so take advantage of this by participating in various clubs, events, and activities to meet people from different backgrounds and cultures. 
2) Different learning style - Western's course structure may differ from what we know at KU. They put emphasis on lectures, assessments, midterms (multiple choice), projects etc. The midterms and exams are multiple choice so it's a lot about memorising the material compared to how it works at KU.
3) Explore Canada - go to different regions! Canada is renowned for its natural beauty and pretty landscapes!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you have saved up some money - London is quite expensive compared to Denmark (in some aspects). And don't hesitate to ask for help - whether it's for academic guidance or otherwise! Secure housing well in advance (but don't commit to anything before seeing the place!), and make sure all your courses are approved before you go. But remember to have fun while you're there and don't focus solely on your studies!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I med during my time there, the friendships I formed (I still speak to a lot of them), and the memories I created are truly unforgettable.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Dealing with all the red tape - getting courses approved and finding suitable accommodation was quite a hassle. But thankfully, I didn't encounter any major challenges while I was there.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
